prerequisites: None explicitly required. However, for a correct understanding and assimilation of the content, it is highly recommended to have completed the first-year mathematics courses: Algebra and Calculus. It is also recommended to be taking or to have taken the Advanced Calculus course, as techniques such as integration methods for multi-variable functions will be applied.

learning_outcomes.text: Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated through the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.

Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge about: linear algebra; geometry; differential geometry; differential and integral calculus; differential and partial differential equations; numerical methods; numerical algorithms, statistics, and optimization.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.

syllabus_topics: Statistical variable types and frequency tables or distributions
Main statistical parameters of centralization and dispersion
Description of data including values in several variables and how to analyze their relationship
Main properties, independence of events, and conditional probability
Random variable concept in one and several dimensions
Most important discrete and continuous probability distributions
Introduction of the concept of statistic and the study of sampling distributions
Estimation techniques for population parameters and Hypothesis Tests
Application of previous concepts to the study of regression models
teaching_methods: Distance education supported by information and communication technologies
Work with theoretical and practical content (consultation of didactic materials, attendance at tutorials, consultations with teaching staff and tutors, participation in the student forum)
Autonomous work (study of theoretical content, solving exercises and problems, and preparation for face-to-face tests)
Completion of evaluation activities (face-to-face test and self-assessment and continuous assessment activities)
Use of virtual course on the aLF platform
assessment_rules: Final grade = Face-to-face exam grade (maximum 9 points) + Continuous Assessment Test (PEC) grade (maximum 1 point). To add the PEC grade, the face-to-face exam grade must be equal to or greater than 4.5 points. If the exam grade is less than 4.5, the final grade will be the face-to-face exam grade only. The face-to-face exam requires a minimum of 5 points to pass without the PEC. If the subject is not passed in the February call, the PEC grade will be taken into account for the September call.
